/-!
# Erdős Problem 481

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/481](https://www.erdosproblems.com/481)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980), p.96.
- [Kl82] Klarner, David A., *A sufficient condition for certain semigroups to be free*.
  J. Algebra (1982), 140-148.
- [KoTa22] Kolpakov, Alexander and Talambutsa, Alexey, *On free semigroups of affine maps on the
  real line*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2022), 2301-2307.
-/

namespace Erdos481

/--
For a finite sequence of $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integers $A = (x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, the
sequence `T a b A` of length $rn$ given by $(a_ix_j+b_i)_{1\leq j\leq n, 1\leq i\leq r}$.
-/
def T {r : ℕ} (a b : Fin r → ℕ) (A : List ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  (List.finRange r).flatMap (fun i : Fin r => A.map (fun x : ℕ => a i * x + b i))

/--
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_r,b_1,\ldots,b_r\in \mathbb{N}$ such that $\sum_{i}\frac{1}{a_i}>1$. For any
finite sequence of $n$ (not necessarily distinct) integers $A=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ let $T(A)$ denote
the sequence of length $rn$ given by
$$(a_ix_j+b_i)_{1\leq j\leq n, 1\leq i\leq r}.$$
Prove that, if $A_1=(1)$ and $A_{i+1}=T(A_i)$, then there must be some $A_k$ with repeated
elements.

This is true. This appears to have first been shown by Klarner [Kl82], with a generalisation
given by Kolpakov and Talambutsa [KoTa22]. Essentially the same proof was found independently by
Barreto in the comment section.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_481 {r : ℕ} (a b : Fin r → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i)
    (hab : 1 < ∑ i, (1 : ℝ) / a i) :
    ∃ k, ¬ ((T a b)^[k] [1]).Nodup := by
  sorry

end Erdos481

reformulations.difference: The helper chooses an i-major enumeration of the doubly indexed family and uses natural-valued lists rather than arbitrary integer lists.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Changing to a j-major enumeration only permutes the output. T preserves list permutations, so the corresponding iterates remain permutation-equivalent and have identical Nodup status. Furthermore, the orbit starting at [1] with natural coefficients stays natural-valued. Casting its entries to integers commutes with T and iteration, and the injective cast preserves Nodup. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch files.

reformulations.difference: The theorem permits b i = 0, whereas the positive-integer reading of the website's statement and its minimum-growth remark excludes zero intercepts.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The universally quantified versions are equivalent. If a generator is the identity (a i = 1 and b i = 0), the reciprocal-sum hypothesis forces r ≥ 2; composing that generator and another generator in either order gives a repetition at iteration 2. Otherwise, h(x) = 2x − 1 fixes 1 and conjugates each map to y ↦ a i*y + (a i + 2*b i − 1), whose intercept is positive. The slopes and reciprocal sum are unchanged, and h is injective on the orbit, so repetitions are preserved. The reverse implication is restriction to positive intercepts. The full equivalence was proved in Lean without using the sorry-backed problem theorem.

sources_consulted: T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #481, including its statement, additional remarks and status: https://www.erdosproblems.com/481, read through the archived 2025-12-29 page at https://web.archive.org/web/20260101000000id_/https://www.erdosproblems.com/481.

Erdős and Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1980), p.96, with context on pp.95–97: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf (scanned pages read using OCR).

Kolpakov and Talambutsa, On free semigroups of affine maps on the real line, arXiv:2105.09387v2, especially Theorem 3 and its proof: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09387 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2105.09387.

Klarner [Kl82] bibliographic metadata: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1016%2F0021-8693(82)90010-2. Its relevant mathematical result was read through the explicit restatement and proof in Kolpakov–Talambutsa, not through Klarner's inaccessible full text.
Author bibliographies used to locate the original book: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/ and https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html.

review.notes: Both declarations were checked. The solved tag agrees with the archived problem page and current database. Tests covered empty lists, impossible r = 0 and r = 1 hypotheses, k = 0, repeated inputs and generators, and concrete collision/noncollision examples. Lean proofs also checked the output length and the harmless shift between iteration k and the source's A_{k+1}. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equiv.lean. The live problem page/forum and Klarner's full text were inaccessible; the archived statement, original book and Kolpakov–Talambutsa supplied sufficient mathematical evidence.
